$comment: How a client holds a session, as every SDK must compute it. `refreshSchedule`: how long to wait before renewing an access token, from its own claims. The margin before expiry is half the token's lifetime (`exp - iat`, or the time remaining when there is no `iat`), capped at 300 seconds; the wait is never under 10 seconds; a token with no readable `exp` schedules nothing (`delay` null). Times are in seconds; a row gives the token's `claims`, which a runner puts in any JWT, or a literal `token`. `tokenExpiry`: reading `exp` out of a token. A JWT's segments are base64url without padding, and its payload is UTF-8, so a reader that assumes plain base64 or ASCII fails for the accounts whose names produce `-`, `_` or a multi-byte character. TypeScript runs this in packages/sdk (session-agreement.test.ts). The Rust SDK runs it when its session lands. The launcher's Go holds a session too (oauth.go, session.go) and does not run this table yet.

refreshSchedule.why: an hour-long token just issued is renewed 300 seconds before it expires: the margin's ceiling
a five-minute token is renewed at half its life, not at once: a fixed 300-second margin equals this lifetime and schedules a renewal for the moment of issue, forever
a one-minute token is renewed at half its life
a ten-minute token sits where half its life equals the ceiling
the margin comes from the lifetime the issuer chose, not from what remains of it
a token past its renewal point waits the floor, never zero
an expired token waits the floor: one attempt per interval, not a loop
a token shorter than twice the floor waits the floor, though that is past its half-life
with no iat the lifetime is what remains, and half of it is still bounded
with no iat and a long time remaining the ceiling applies
a token with no exp schedules nothing
a token that is not a JWT schedules nothing

tokenExpiry.why: an ASCII payload, whose length is not a multiple of four: JWTs omit the padding
a payload whose base64url spelling contains `_`: the name is Zoë Fauré
a payload whose base64url spelling contains `-`: the name is O’Connor, with a typographic apostrophe
two segments are not a JWT
a payload that is not base64url
a payload that is not JSON
